## Overview

LRPGBL03 models the **achievement level of not-directly-taught receptive
vocabulary** (`b1rent`) — the Block 1 not-taught receptive score at a given
timepoint. It is the level companion to [LRPGBG03](../lrp-rli-gbg-003/index.qmd) (gain) and the
generalisation counterpart to the taught level [LRPGBL01](../lrp-rli-gbl-001/index.qmd). Added in
#116 Phase B.

This is a **baseline exploratory model**. It was Huber-tuned by Optuna on the full
predictor set (150 trials, seed 47; Huber retune of 2026-09-22, superseding #169), running on the full `Predictors.DEFAULT_LEVEL`
set (the target `b1rent` is already excluded), with no outlier exclusion. As a level model a high naive
R² is partly concurrent same-construct correlation — read the ranking as
exploratory.

::: {.callout-note title="Leakage exclusion: b1reto"}

The Block 1 receptive *total* `b1reto` equals taught + not-taught
(`b1retau + b1rent`), so it contains the target directly and is removed. The
standardised receptive (`rowpvt`) and expressive (`eowpvt`) tests are *retained* in
this baseline and kept in the full set. (The not-taught denominator, ~12
items, is unconfirmed, #144.)

:::

Cross-validation is group-aware (`GroupKFold`, grouped by `subject_id`).

This model identifies predictive associations and possible interactions. The Bayesian models examine specific questions with uncertainty. Only contrasts supported by the study design and stated assumptions receive a causal interpretation.

::: {.callout-important title="Exploratory — associational, not causal"}
The importance rankings and SHAP directions below describe associations in these data, not causal effects: a high-ranking predictor is not necessarily a useful target for intervention, and `same_skill_of_outcome` flags any predictor that concurrently restates the outcome. A Bayesian model also needs a suitable design and assumptions before a contrast can be interpreted causally.
:::

## Validation

### Cross-validation

Cross-validation holds out whole children, so one child's timepoints cannot appear in both training and validation data. Hyperparameters were selected using these same grouped folds. The results therefore describe performance after tuning within this dataset; they are not an independent estimate of performance in new data.

The headline metrics combine the held-out predictions from all folds. R² compares their squared errors with a baseline that predicts each fold's training-set mean. Neither prediction uses the held-out child's outcomes for fitting.

```{python}
#| output: asis
import json

with open("metrics.json") as _f:
    _metrics = json.load(_f)

_pooled_labels = {
    "cv_pooled_mae": "MAE",
    "cv_pooled_rmse": "RMSE",
    "cv_pooled_r2": "R²",
    "cv_pooled_medae": "MedAE",
}
print("| Pooled OOF metric (post-selection) | Value |")
print("|:---|---:|")
for _k, _label in _pooled_labels.items():
    _v = _metrics.get(_k)
    print(f"| {_label} | {_v:.4f} |" if _v is not None else f"| {_label} | n/a |")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
import pandas as pd

cv_scores = pd.read_csv("cv_scores.csv")
if not bool(_metrics.get("cv_r2_per_fold_reliable", False)):
    _note = _metrics.get(
        "cv_r2_note",
        "Per-fold R² is unstable on the small held-out folds of "
        "near-leave-one-subject-out CV; use the pooled OOF metrics above.",
    )
    print(
        f"::: {{.callout-warning title=\"Per-fold summaries unreliable\"}}\n"
        f"{_note}\n:::\n"
    )
print("Per-fold mean ± SD (secondary; the pooled OOF metrics above are the headline):\n")
for _col in ["mae", "rmse", "r2", "medae"]:
    _label = _col.upper() if _col != "r2" else "R²"
    print(f"- {_label}: {cv_scores[_col].mean():.4f} ± {cv_scores[_col].std():.4f}")
```

### In-sample evaluation

```{python}
eval_df = pd.read_csv("evaluation.csv")

y_true = eval_df["y_true"]
y_pred = eval_df["y_pred"]
abs_resid = (y_true - y_pred).abs()
sq_error = (y_true - y_pred) ** 2

mae = abs_resid.mean()
rmse = sq_error.mean() ** 0.5
medae = abs_resid.median()
ss_res = sq_error.sum()
ss_tot = ((y_true - y_true.mean()) ** 2).sum()
r2 = 1.0 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot > 0 else float("nan")

print(f"In-sample MAE:   {mae:.4f}")
print(f"In-sample RMSE:  {rmse:.4f}")
print(f"In-sample R²:    {r2:.4f}")
print(f"In-sample MedAE: {medae:.4f}")
```

## Feature importance

### Permutation importance

Permutation importance measures how much prediction error increases when a predictor is shuffled between children. Each child receives a donor child's values at matching assessment waves. Donors must have the same observed-wave schedule, so this measures importance conditional on that schedule. Children with a unique schedule cannot move; `permutation_schedule_support.csv` reports that limitation. Each fold predicts only its held-out children; the predictions are then combined to calculate one root mean squared error (RMSE) per shuffle. Importance is measured in RMSE units. The models use a Huber objective and RMSE scoring. Huber limits the residual gradient beyond its threshold, but its predictions need not be conditional means for skewed or floored outcomes. RMSE-based importance measures how much these fitted predictions worsen under the specified shuffle. The table lists every predictor; the box plot shows the ten with the largest mean importance.

```{python}
#| output: asis
from language_reading_predictors.models._reporting import gb_permutation_support_markdown

print(gb_permutation_support_markdown("."))
```


```{python}
perm_imp = pd.read_csv("permutation_importance.csv")
perm_imp
```
The box plot shows the variation across shuffles. Positive importance means shuffling increased prediction error; a value near zero means the model changed little under the permitted shuffles. Missing importance means the predictor is not assessable under this design. This spread is not a credible interval for a causal effect.

![Permutation importances](permutation_importance.png){#fig-perm-importance .lightbox fig-align="left"}

### SHAP analysis

The bar plots show the ten predictors with the largest mean |SHAP| and collapse the rest into one "other features" row.

![SHAP bar plot](shap_bar.png){#fig-shap-bar .lightbox fig-align="left"}

![SHAP summary plot](shap_summary.png){#fig-shap-summary .lightbox fig-align="left"}

#### Waterfall plot (most representative observation)

SHAP waterfall plot for the most representative observation (lowest combined
residual and distance from the median feature vector), showing how each feature
pushes the prediction from the base value.

![SHAP waterfall plot](shap_waterfall.png){#fig-shap-waterfall .lightbox fig-align="left"}

#### Waterfall plots at the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the outcome

One waterfall for each of the three observations whose observed outcome lies nearest the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the fitted target (ties go to the observation the model fits best), showing how the leading predictors move the prediction from the base value for a low, a typical and a high scorer. Each waterfall names its ten largest contributions and pools the rest. The table records which child-wave each plot explains, with the observed and predicted values.

## Predictor ranking and clustering

The ranking groups predictors with similar variation, using distance correlation. Groups are ordered by their combined held-out permutation importance, then predictors are ordered within each group. `same_skill_of_outcome` marks measures that restate the outcome at the same wave. These tables are produced at the `test` and `reporting` tiers.

## SHAP interactions

The table and heatmap show how much each predictor pair's joint contribution to the prediction differs from the sum of its separate contributions. Each value sums the mean absolute SHAP interactions in the `[i, j]` and `[j, i]` entries. A larger value indicates more interaction in the fitted prediction model, not a causal interaction.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
shap_interactions = (
    pd.read_csv("shap_interactions.csv").head(12) if Path("shap_interactions.csv").exists()
    else pd.DataFrame({"note": ["shap_interactions.csv is produced at the reporting/test tiers"]})
)
shap_interactions
```
